title: Get your home ready for winter
intro: An autumn checklist to get through winter without nasty surprises.

steps.t: Turn the heating on and feel each radiator: if it's cold at the top, bleed it (see the bleed-a-radiator guide).
steps.q: Are all radiators warm from top to bottom?
steps.fix: Bleed the ones that are cold at the top (see the bleed-a-radiator guide), then recheck the boiler pressure.

steps.t: Hunt for draughts: run the back of your hand along windows and doors on a windy day.
Where you feel air, clean the frame and stick on draught strip. Under the door, use a draught excluder.
Close the indoor valve for the outside tap if there is one, then open the tap outside to drain it.
Fit the insulating cover over the outside tap and disconnect the garden hose.
Check the gutters from the ground: leaves, plants or overflowing water. If they need clearing, get help or call someone.
Press the test button on every smoke and CO alarm until it sounds.
steps.fix: Change the battery and test again. If it stays silent or is past the replace-by date on its label, replace it.

steps.t: Find the date of the boiler's last service in its logbook or on the label.
steps.q: Was the boiler serviced in the last 12 months?
steps.fix: Book a qualified engineer before the cold sets in. How often depends on the model and local rules.

steps.t: Check the boiler pressure: usually [[1-1.5 bar]] with the system cold.
Find the main water stopcock and check it turns: you'll need it fast if a pipe bursts.

tips: Do it in October, before the frosts: by December engineers are fully booked.
Pipes in an unheated garage, cellar or loft? Wrap them in foam pipe lagging: it's cheap.

title: Smell gas at home: what to do
intro: Smell gas? A few actions, in the right order, to get everyone safe.

steps.t: No flames: don't light the hob, lighters or matches, and don't smoke.
steps.w: A single spark or flame can ignite the gas.

steps.t: Don't touch switches, plugs or doorbells: leave on what's on and off what's off.
steps.w: Even switching something off can make a spark: don't touch anything electrical.

steps.t: Open doors and windows wide straight away.
Close the gas valve at the meter only if it's close and safe to reach: turn the lever across the pipe.
Get out and get everyone out, pets too. Leave the door open.
steps.fix: Call them from outside. Don't go back in to look for them: tell the emergency services straight away.

steps.t: Only once you're outside, away from the house, call 999 in the UK, 911 in the US, 112 in the EU.
Don't go back in until the fire service or the gas engineer says it's safe.

tips: If the smell is faint and you're not sure, get out and call anyway: let the operator decide.
Fit a certified gas detector near the boiler and cooker: it warns you before you can smell it.

title: Clean the gutters
intro: Leaf-clogged gutters spill water down your walls: clear them with a ladder and a bucket.
gate: Someone is with me to hold the ladder

steps.t: From the ground, see where the gutter is blocked and check there are no power lines nearby.
steps.w: Keep the ladder well away from overhead power lines: it's dangerous even without touching them.

steps.t: Stand the ladder on firm, level ground. On soft soil, put a board under the feet.
Set the angle: for every [[4 m]] of height, the foot goes [[1 m]] out from the wall.
steps.q: Is the foot about [[1 m]] out for every [[4 m]] of height?
steps.fix: Move the foot until it is. If the feet slip or the ladder wobbles, don't climb.

steps.t: Have someone hold the ladder, hang the bucket on the S-hook and climb, always holding on with one hand.
steps.w: Only climb with someone holding the ladder, and keep two feet and one hand on it at all times.

steps.t: Only work within arm's reach, belly between the rails. Any further: climb down and move the ladder.
steps.w: Never lean out sideways: that's how ladders slide.

steps.t: Wearing gloves, scoop leaves and sludge towards you and drop them into the bucket.
Climb down, empty the bucket into a bag, move the ladder and repeat along the whole gutter.
Flush the gutter with the hose from the end farthest from the downpipe: water should run to the outlet.
Look down: water should gush out of the bottom of the downpipe.
steps.q: Does water flow out of the bottom of the downpipe, not back up?
steps.fix: If it backs up, the downpipe is blocked: try flushing it from the bottom. If it won't clear, call a pro.

steps.t: Look for drips at the joints and bent brackets: they need repairing.

tips: Gutters higher than the first floor? Call a professional instead of climbing that high.
Fit a mesh gutter guard after cleaning: far fewer leaves get in.
Pick a dry, calm day after the last leaves have fallen.

title: Boiler not working: what to do
intro: Boiler locked out or no heat? What you can check yourself and who to call.
why: A boiler burns gas and vents fumes: a wrong fix can cause leaks or carbon monoxide. Only certified engineers may work on it.

steps.t: Check the thermostat and power: turn the thermostat up, check its batteries and see if the boiler display is on.
Read the pressure gauge: with the system cold it's usually [[1-1.5 bar]].
steps.q: Is the pressure in the right range?
steps.fix: If it's low and the manual shows how to top it up, do it. Otherwise tell the engineer the reading.

steps.t: Press the reset button once only, as the manual says. If it locks out again, stop.
steps.w: Reset only once: repeated resets on a boiler that keeps locking out can be dangerous.

steps.t: Write down the error code, plus the make and model from the label: take a photo.
Never open the casing: call a Gas Safe registered engineer in the UK, or a licensed technician.
steps.w: Inside are gas, flue gases and mains power: only the engineer opens the casing.

tips: Smell gas or the CO alarm goes off? Get out and call for help: see the Smell gas guide.
Book the service in autumn: lots of faults show up on the first cold day.
